summary: Eight 12x14 modules on kit 1's exact lane grid. Each is a recognisable Southern vernacular type: a log dogtrot with an open breezeway, an ochre camelback, a white two-storey I-house with a gallery porch and end chimneys, a pyramid-roofed four-room cottage, an oxblood board-and-batten boarding house, a smokehouse work yard, a pecan and bee orchard, and a brick 1920s bungalow. No wall wood or roof material repeats kit 1, so a mixed street varies. Eight 12x14 plots on the kit-1 grid: dogtrot, camelback, I-house, pyramid cottage, boarding house, work yard, pecan orchard and bee yard, 1920s bungalow. Each house has its own wall wood and roof colour, none repeating kit 1. Six trade-cut parts; 28 rooms for furnishers; chimneys use chimney(), stairs use flight().

concept_subject: A sunlit row along a gravel mill-village lane with wheel ruts and a lantern post every 12 blocks. Each plot is fronted by a picket fence with a centred gate. From west to east: (0) a dogtrot house made of two dark oak-log pens under one brown weathered-tin side-gable roof. An open breezeway runs through the middle behind a full-width porch, and a fieldstone chimney rises at the back. (1) A narrow ochre-yellow clapboard camelback shotgun with white corner boards and oxblood shutters. It has a front-gable galvanized-tin roof, and behind it a taller two-storey hump with its own gable, with a brick chimney on the west side. (2) The overseer's I-house: tall, white, one room deep, with a symmetrical three-bay front and dark green shutters. It has a full-width two-storey porch with pale posts, a railed upper gallery, a quartz cornice, a dark slate side-gable roof and slim brick end chimneys running up both white gables. (3) A square four-room mill cottage with grey-white weatherboard and a red-tin pyramid roof. A single brick chimney rises from its apex, and a porch runs across the front. (4) A long two-storey oxblood board-and-batten boarding house with pale battens and a belt course. It has six upper windows over a long shed-roofed porch with rocking chairs, a hanging BOARDING sign, an olive-grey tin roof and a chimney at the west end. (5) A fenced packed-dirt work yard. It holds a small log smokehouse with a sooty black roof and a smoke vent at the back, with hams hanging inside. There is a woodpile under a slab lean-to, a wash kettle (cauldron) over a sunk campfire with rinse barrels, and a bench. (6) A pecan orchard of three broad, flat-crowned trees. It has a picnic table with benches, a chain swing hanging from a low limb, and a row of four beehives among cornflowers and daisies, with a wild bee nest under a branch. (7) A 1920s red-brick bungalow under a low green front-gable roof that sweeps over a deep porch. The porch has tapered posts on brick pedestals, white trim, paired windows, a louvred gable vent and exposed rafter tails, with a brick chimney on the west slope.
